name: Province of British Columbia
source: Visual Identity Program, 1977: the General, Reproduction, Sign and Vehicle manuals, as rebuilt in the BC manual pack (manuals/bc); the Provincial Symbol from PofBC’s reconstruction.
status: A historical reconstruction for reference and study. Not the Province’s current identity, which is published by the Government of British Columbia.

print.note: The program names Pantone 462 (brown) for print and gives paint, decal and sign-material references (Reproduction Manual p. 28). Screen colours are approximations.

positive.label: Two colours: brown symbol, black type

italic.label: Helvetica Regular Italic (TeX Gyre Heros Italic)

light.label: Helvetica Ultra Light (set in Regular: no open Ultra Light)

typography.note: Helvetica Medium for the provincial logotype, Helvetica Regular for ministerial logotypes and component designations, upper and lower case; capitals only for branches and split ministries (General Manual p. 6; Reproduction Manual p. 12).

symbol.name: provincial-symbol
symbol.title: Provincial Symbol
symbol.masterDescription: The Provincial Coat of Arms within its band: positive form. The manual’s reverse form is separate artwork (the Union Jack stays black and the Sun white); this reconstruction has the positive form only.

signatures.label: Provincial signature
signatures.use: The symbol with the provincial logotype alone: covers, the Province as a whole (General Manual pp. 3–5).

sources.title: Provincial Signature: Grid Layout: Positive Form

signatures.label: Flush-left, horizontal
signatures.use: Stationery and advertising. The ministry in two or more lines to the right of the logotype; component and address below a 1 point rule.

sources.title: Symbol and Signature Format Use; repro-sheet guide
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

signatures.label: Flush-left, vertical
signatures.use: Top left or bottom left on the front or back covers of publications; advertisements.

sources.title: Symbol and Signature Format Use; repro-sheet guide
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements
Symbol and Signature Format Use; repro-sheet guide
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

signatures.label: Centred
signatures.use: Posters, brochures, back covers of books, large advertisements.

sources.title: Symbol and Signature Format Use; repro-sheet guide
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

signatures.label: One line
signatures.use: Stationery and advertising where depth is short.

sources.title: Symbol and Signature Format Use; repro-sheet guide
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

signatures.label: Signs: centred
signatures.use: Primary identification signs only (Sign Manual p. 8, fig. 1): the upper half of the sign.

sources.title: Sign Repro: Positive Form; Grid System; charts

signatures.label: Signs: horizontal
signatures.use: Standard information, warning and regulatory signs (Sign Manual p. 8, fig. 2): the signature band at the foot.

sources.title: Sign Repro: Positive Form; Grid System; charts

signatures.label: Uniform insignia
signatures.use: Patches, crests and badges on uniforms (General Manual p. 13): the symbol over the logotype on two lines, the ministry beneath.

signatures.label: Vehicles: door marking
signatures.use: Driver and passenger doors (Vehicle Manual p. 3): a 5 in symbol over a ½ in logotype and a 1 in ministry name, centred and centre-marked.

lockup.clearspaceRecommendation: The signature is reproduced as it appears in the manual: never modified, never with another design superimposed, and the symbol never without the provincial logotype.

patterns.name: Dogwood repeat
patterns.description: Complete six-bract flowers repeat in a measured, alternating rhythm. A new geometric interpretation of Pacific dogwood.
patterns.title: {name} / Dogwood repeat / supporting study

patterns.name: Petal mosaic
patterns.description: Single bracts turn through six directions at three scales, with a recurring gold accent.
patterns.title: {name} / Petal mosaic / supporting study

patterns.name: Measured rules
patterns.description: Fine paired rules and short registration ticks borrow the discipline of the manuals’ measured layouts.
patterns.title: {name} / Measured rules / supporting study

patterns.name: Contour bands
patterns.description: Parallel curves suggest terrain and a shifting coastline without representing a measured map.
patterns.title: {name} / Contour bands / supporting study

patterns.name: Rule lattice
patterns.description: Offset bundles of diagonal rules form a woven field, with one gold course in each repeat.
patterns.title: {name} / Rule lattice / supporting study

patterns.name: Dogwood bower
patterns.description: Flowers in several sizes frame an open centre. A focal composition for a cover or invitation.
patterns.title: {name} / Dogwood bower / supporting study

patterns.name: Seed field
patterns.description: Tiny flowers punctuate an even field of dots. A quiet texture for reverse sides and borders.
patterns.title: {name} / Seed field / supporting study

patterns.name: Stepped courses
patterns.description: Broad stepped forms alternate direction and scale to make a bold geometric repeat.
patterns.title: {name} / Stepped courses / supporting study

templates.description: A title page (General Manual p. 8): flush-left vertical signature top left, a rule, then the title in Helvetica Regular. The manual prints no sizes; proportions are measured from its drawing.

Dental and

templates.title: Province of British Columbia / title page with publication statement

elements.text:
Special Report on the
Effects of Tourism

templates.label: Advertisement: tender
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / standard tender advertisement
templates.description: A standard operative advertisement (General Manual p. 9): subject and the word Tender between 1 point rules, copy, and the flush-left horizontal signature beneath. Proportions measured from the drawing.

elements.text: Sealed tenders for the work described will be received by the undersigned until 2:00 p.m., [date]. Tender documents may be obtained from the address below.

templates.label: Advertisement: one-column announcement
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / one-column announcement
templates.description: A narrow newspaper announcement (General Manual p. 9): head, copy, and the centred ministerial signature at the foot over a closing rule.

elements.text: [Announcement copy, set in one newspaper column.]

templates.label: Shoulder flash: job function
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / shoulder flash, job function
templates.description: A shield-shaped shoulder flash (General Manual p. 13): white field, brown outline, the job function in a band at the top, and the stacked ministerial signature, positive.

templates.label: Shoulder flash: security
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / shoulder flash, security
templates.description: A brown shoulder flash with a black band (General Manual p. 13): the function reversed in the band, the provincial signature reversed beneath.

templates.label: Vehicle door marking
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / vehicle door marking
templates.description: The ministerial signature on a driver’s or passenger’s door (Vehicle Manual pp. 3–5): a 5 in symbol, ½ in logotype, 1 in ministry name; centred on the door, 2 in below the edge of its upper panel. White on a brown body.

templates.label: Van truck, box side
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / van truck box side
templates.description: A van truck’s box (Vehicle Manual pp. 10–11): a 16 in provincial signature in the top rear corner, 16 in from the edge and 8 in from the top; a 4 in unit number in the top front corner, 8 in from top and side. Black on a white or aluminium box.

sources.title: Vehicle Markings: pickup, sedan, box truck

templates.label: Van truck, rear doors
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / van truck rear doors
templates.description: The rear of a van truck’s box (Vehicle Manual pp. 10–11): the provincial signature centred on the top of the left door, 8 in down; the unit number top right of the right door, 8 in from top and side; 4 in reflective stripes 16 in long, 4 in apart, starting 8 in from the bottom, six to a door.

sources.title: Vehicle Markings: pickup, sedan, box truck

templates.label: Sign: primary identification, 4 × 8 ft
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / primary identification sign
templates.description: Primary identification (Sign Manual pp. 10–11): centred. The ministerial signature, centred format, fills the upper half; a hairline at mid-height; the facility’s name, centred, capitals at most one grid square, in the lower half. Grid square y = 8 in.

templates.label: Sign: standard information, 4 × 8 ft
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / standard information sign
templates.description: Standard information (Sign Manual pp. 14–15): a one-line title, capitals one grid square; the message, its size set by its length (Chart B); a hairline at 5 y and the horizontal ministerial signature in the 1 y band below. All flush left at 0.75 y.

elements.text: Seedlings for the province’s reforestation are grown here. Visitors welcome weekdays.

sources.title: Information signs: message dimensions and body-copy chart

templates.label: Sign: secondary identification blade
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / secondary identification blade
templates.description: Secondary identification (Sign Manual pp. 12–13): one facility per 12 in × 8 ft blade, flush left; 6 in capitals, 3 in margins above and below, 6 in from the left.

templates.label: Sign: secondary directional, four blades
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / secondary directional sign
templates.description: Secondary directional blades (Sign Manual pp. 16–17), for low-speed areas: one destination per blade. Arrows pointing up or left sit at the left with the copy 10 in in; arrows pointing right sit at the right with the copy flush right. 6 in copy and arrows, 3 in margins.

templates.label: Sign: warning, 2 × 4 ft
templates.title: Province of British Columbia / warning sign
templates.description: Warning (Sign Manual pp. 20–21): yellow with black graphics; a short title, capitals one grid square; a bold message; a hairline at 11 y and the horizontal ministerial signature beneath. Grid square y = 4 in.

elements.text: Rodent control in progress. Keep children and pets away from bait stations.

templates.label: Sign: regulatory, 2 × 4 ft

templates.description: Regulatory (Sign Manual pp. 20–21): white with black graphics, the symbol in its prescribed colour (a red STOP octagon); title and message; the ministerial signature always required. Grid square y = 4 in.

intro.headline:
Province of
British Columbia
intro.body: The Province’s 1977 identity, reconstructed from its four manuals: the Provincial Symbol, the ministerial signature for every ministry, Helvetica, Pantone 462, and the stationery, forms, publications, vehicles and signs built on them. A historical reference, not the Province’s current identity.
intro.footer: Province of British Columbia Visual Identity Program, 1977. A reconstruction for reference; not the current provincial identity.

landing.headline:
Province of
British Columbia
1977
landing.body: A reconstruction of the 1977 Visual Identity Program.
landing.contactBody: For the Province’s current identity, see the Government of British Columbia.

The ranch was purchased and cleared of debris and fenced by the Fish & Wildlife Branch to
remove grazing by domestic cattle and sheep and facilitate the recovery of the Bighorn
sheep. This area is also used by Mule Deer, White-tailed Deer, and Elk.

pages.title: The provincial signature.
pages.name: The provincial signature
pages.subtitle: The Provincial Symbol, the coat of arms within its band, with the provincial logotype. Never the symbol alone; never modified.

elements.text: The Provincial Coat of Arms surrounded by a band to focus attention upon it.
The name of the Province, and of the ministry, in Helvetica: Medium for the Province, Regular for the ministry.
Symbol and logotype combined in a specific format. The provincial signature is the symbol with the provincial logotype; the ministerial signature adds the ministry.

Reproduce the signature only as the manuals show it, from the reproduction sheets. Nothing is superimposed on it, and the symbol never appears without the provincial logotype (General Manual pp. 3–4).

sources.title: Provincial Signature: Grid Layout: Positive Form

pages.title: Ministerial signatures.
pages.name: Ministerial signature formats
pages.subtitle: One set of formats for every ministry, set on a single grid. The flush-left formats are standard; one line and centred are alternates.

elements.text: Ministry names are upper and lower case, on two or more lines in the flush-left formats. Branches and split ministries are in capitals, smaller, at the ministry’s x-height. Component and address go below a 1 point rule.

pages.title: One grid for every line.
pages.name: Line spacing
pages.subtitle: Cap height (c) and x-height (x) set every space in the signature, so a ministry of any length keeps the same relationships.

rows: Baseline to baseline within a group
about 4 c, the depth of three lines
Symbol to logotype; logotype to ministry column
Below the ministry, a 1 point rule, then component and address

sources.title: Provincial Signature: Grid Layout: Positive Form
Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

pages.title: Colour.
pages.name: Colour
pages.subtitle: Pantone 462, provincial brown, is the program’s colour. Solid colour only: no screens, no tints.

elements.text: The symbol and band are always one colour. In both forms the Union Jack is black and the Sun white: the reverse form is its own artwork, never an inversion of the positive (not reconstructed here).

pages.title: Helvetica.
pages.name: Typography
pages.subtitle: Two styles: Medium for the provincial logotype, Regular for ministry and component designations. Upper and lower case throughout.

elements.text: Ministry of Lands, Parks and Housing
BRANCHES AND SPLIT MINISTRIES: CAPITALS, SMALLER

Capitals are used only for branches and split ministries. Hand lettering is not recommended. Display type may be photo-lettered or dry-transfer Helvetica; all must match the British Columbia Helvetica Medium standard (Reproduction Manual p. 9). This reconstruction sets Helvetica in TeX Gyre Heros.

sources.title: Typography; stationery, vehicle and sign arrangements

pages.title: Stationery.
pages.name: Stationery
pages.subtitle: One grid for letterhead, envelope and calling card at every rank but the Premier’s and Special Use, which are centred.

elements.text: Ranks: Premier · Ministers (OFFICE OF THE MINISTER) · Deputy Ministers · Boards and Commissions · General Use · Special Use. Format A typesets the component and address above the rule; Format B types them below it.

sources.title: Stationery: Format A; envelopes; calling cards

pages.title: Forms, publications and advertising.
pages.name: Documents
pages.subtitle: The memorandum and news release carry the signature in a brown band. Every advertisement carries the ministerial signature.

pages.title: Vehicles.
pages.name: Vehicles
pages.subtitle: Every vehicle carries the ministerial signature on its doors, the provincial signature on its rear, and a unit number. White markings, or black on white bodies.

rows: 5 in symbol, ½ in logotype, 1 in ministry
16 in signature, 16 in from the edge, 8 in down
2 in on cars and cabs, 4 in on boxes and trailers

sources.title: Vehicle Markings: pickup, sedan, box truck

pages.title: Signs.
pages.name: Signs
pages.subtitle: A grid square of one twelfth of the longest side sets every sign. Brown for information, identification and direction; yellow for warning; white for regulation.

elements.text: EVERY FORMAT, SET FOR ONE MINISTRY. THE KIT CARRIES THEM FOR EVERY MINISTRY OF 1976–1986.
Province of British Columbia / ADDITIONAL SUPPORTING STUDIES
New geometric studies informed by the source identity. Historical symbols and manual guidance remain unchanged.
Use one pattern family per surface. Small repeats give texture; larger fields suit covers and displays. Keep small text and the complete identifying logo on a clear ground.

rules.title: The symbol is never altered.
rules.text: It may arrive, but its proportions, its colour and the arms within the band never change. Every logo study ends on the official signature.

rules.title: Ceremony, not effects.
rules.text: Measured timings and plain eases, as befits the Province’s seal: no bounces, spins, blurs or glows.

rules.title: Loops are for waiting.
rules.text: Only the band loops, never the full signature, and only while something loads.

rules.title: Still is a valid frame.
rules.text: With reduced motion, every study shows its final frame. Nothing depends on the animation to be understood.

studies.name: Seal
studies.timing: slow, then base and slow · settle
studies.description: The band is pressed into place like a seal, the arms come up inside it, then the Province’s name rises beneath.

studies.name: Arms
studies.use: Explaining the symbol, longer title sequences
studies.description: With the band in place, the arms are assembled part by part, top to bottom: crown, lion, shield, supporters.

studies.name: Unveil
studies.description: The signature is uncovered from the top down, the way a sign’s cover comes away.

studies.name: Band
studies.use: Page and app loading, 32 px and up
studies.description: The band pulses slowly while the arms hold still. Symbol only; stops when loading ends.

studies.name: Sign
studies.use: Video end cards, slide transitions, kiosk screens
studies.description: A brown panel rises into the frame like a highway sign, and the signature appears on it in white.

patternCollection.description: New supporting studies informed by the kit’s brown, gold and cream palette, the manuals’ measured layouts and British Columbia’s Pacific dogwood. The floral forms are new geometric drawings, not reproductions of an official emblem. The identifying coat of arms remains complete and upright.
